birth:jesus_905@7d6db1.note: Matthew 2:1 places the birth in Herod's days; Luke 2:7 records it. The year, 4 BC (-3), comes from outside chronology.

date:between-the-testaments@524500.note: Scripture records no events in this gap. Malachi (1:1) closes the Old Testament; Luke 1:5 is the next dated scene, in Herod's days. Both bounds are outside dating.

date:birth-of-job@af497d.note: Scripture never gives Job's birth; Job 42:16 gives 140 more years after his restoration. The year -1719 (1720 BC) is outside dating.

date:death-of-moses@957d63.note: Deuteronomy 34:5 records his death in Moab; 34:7 gives his age, 120. Scripture gives no BC year; -1451 (1452 BC) is outside dating.

date:divided-kingdom@2c7e3d.note: Solomon's death and Rehoboam's succession (1 Kings 11:43), the split (12:19-20), and Samaria's fall (2 Kings 17:6) are stated. The BC years are outside dating.

date:early-church@a90e19.note: Pentecost (2:1), the witness to the uttermost part (1:8), and the road to Rome (28:14) are stated. AD 30 and AD 96 are outside dating.

date:exiles@d4e1be.note: Stated: Assyria's carrying away (2 Kings 17:6), Babylon's siege (25:1), the temple burned (25:9), and Cyrus's first year (Ezra 1:1). The BC years are outside dating.

date:exodus@5ea65a.note: Exodus 12:41 says Israel left at the end of 430 years; Joshua 4:1 has the Jordan crossed; Deuteronomy 1:3 gives the fortieth year. BC years are outside dating.

date:israel-in-egypt@85a626.note: Exodus 12:40-41 says the sojourn in Egypt lasted 430 years, ending the day Israel left. These dates span about 216 years, so they contradict the text's length.

date:judges@4ee86b.note: Joshua 4:1 has Israel crossing the Jordan; Judges 16:31 gives Samson's twenty years; 1 Samuel 10:1 anoints Saul. Years like -1450 and -1094 are outside dating.

date:life-of-christ@e5a8ac.note: Luke 1:5-13 places John's announced birth in Herod's days; Luke 3:1 dates the ministry to Tiberius's fifteenth year; John 19:30 records his death. -5 and 30 are outside dating.

date:patriarchs@130aac.note: Terah begets Abram at 70 (11:26); Abram leaves Haran at 75 (12:4); Jacob enters Egypt (46:6). Ages, not BC years, are given; -1995 and -1706 are outside dating.

date:return@9b1605.note: Stated: Cyrus's first year (Ezra 1:1), the temple done in Darius's sixth (6:15), Artaxerxes' 32nd (Neh 13:6). The description's c. 432 BC does not match -430 (431 BC).

date:united-kingdom-era@b63762.note: Saul is anointed 'captain' (1 Sam 10:1); David first reigns over Judah only (2 Sam 2:4); Solomon's death ends it (1 Kings 11:43). The BC years are outside dating.

death:jesus_905@22ede5.note: John 19:30 records the death; Luke 3:1 dates the ministry to Tiberius's fifteenth year. AD 30 is not stated and rests on outside dating.

lede:between-the-testaments@44033c.note: No count of four centuries or Maccabees in Scripture. Daniel 8:21 and 11:2 foretell Greece and Persia; Scripture says nothing of Rome taking hold here.
